papers.what_it_is: A theory paper defining shadow models (quantum-trained, classically evaluated QML models), proving they are universally captured by flipped linear models, sit strictly between BPP and BQP under complexity assumptions, and give a learning advantage on a discrete-cube-root task.

existing.note: Theorem 5 also states the class: non-shadowfiable means not in BPP/qgenpoly. Its formal proof (Lemma D.2) shows that if all quantum models were shadowfiable with error below 0.15 and probability at least 2/3, BQP would be contained in P/poly. Fuller quotes are given; the stored quote was cut short.
existing.value: The paper proves that, under the assumption that BQP is not contained in P/poly, there exist quantum models (models in BQP) that are not shadowfiable, that is, not in BPP/qgenpoly; formally, if all quantum models were shadowfiable to error below 0.15 with probability at least 2/3 over the shadowing phase, then BQP would be contained in P/poly.

assertions.value: The paper defines a general shadow model as a classical polynomial-time algorithm that takes a new input together with advice made of computational-basis measurement outcomes of polynomial-time quantum circuits; the advice must be independent of the future inputs.

papers.what_it_is: A mathematical paper giving sufficient conditions, stated as theorems on block structure of graph-Laplacian density operators, for pure states and for zero quantum discord of weighted-graph quantum states.

existing.note: The theorem's condition is that the density operator is a sum of terms p_i ρi1 ⊗ ρi2 with ρi1 and ρi2 commuting, not 'two commuting-block terms'. The full statement is quoted; the proof is a one-line appeal to the cited Huang et al. criterion.
existing.value: The paper states, for the density operator of a weighted graph representing an n-qubit state, that the quantum discord is zero if the density operator can be written as a weighted sum of tensor products ρi1 ⊗ ρi2 with ρi1 and ρi2 commuting; the proof appeals to a cited criterion.
quotes: The quantum discord is zero, if the density operator can be expressed as ρG = i piρi1 ⊗ ρi2, with the condition that ρi1 and ρi2 commute.
(The normality and commutativity of blocks of the density operator imply that the quantum discord is zero [16].)
existing.certainty_reason: Proof rests on a cited result and is not developed in the paper; the summation sign is lost in the text layer.

existing.reader_inference: Although the aim names necessary and sufficient conditions, every zero-discord theorem in Sec. 3 is stated as a sufficient ('if') condition only.

papers.what_it_is: A framework pairing shot-count-aware estimators with sensitivity-analysed optimizers for variational quantum algorithms, with error bounds and two simulated case studies (error-aware simulated annealing; recursive estimator with gradient descent).

existing.note: The gains are shown only in simulation on a one-qubit benchmark (Rx and Z, cost cos θ) and, for the second case, also on MaxCut for a 4-vertex square graph; comparators are simple fixed-error simulated annealing and the plain sample mean estimator.
existing.value: The authors report that in both case studies the proposed approach yields notable performance enhancements over conventional methods, shown in simulations on a one-qubit benchmark problem and, for the recursive estimator, also on MaxCut for a square graph with 4 vertices and 4 edges.
quotes: In both instances, we demonstrate that our proposed approach yields notable performance enhancements compared to conventional methods.
Assume a variational task with one qubit and U (θ) = Rx(θ) and O = Z with C = I
the same experiment has also been carried out on the more complex MaxCut problem for a square graph (|V | = 4 and |E| = 4).
existing.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study, small simulated problems, results shown in figures only.
existing.reader_inference: No device noise beyond shot noise is modelled; no quantitative shot savings are stated in the text.

existing.note: The paper does derive the bounds: Theorem 1 bounds MSE and confidence interval of the sample mean estimator in terms of shot counts, and Algorithm 1 approximately solves the sufficient-shots problem by relaxing MSE to these bounds and allowing real-valued shot counts.
existing.value: The authors derive bounds (Theorem 1) on the mean squared error and confidence interval of the sample mean estimator in terms of shot numbers, and give Algorithm 1, which approximately solves the sufficient-number-of-shots optimisation by relaxing the MSE to these bounds and letting shot counts take real values.

papers.what_it_is: Proposes the Hamiltonian QAOA (HamQAOA) for local Hamiltonian problems, with a symmetry-breaking driver, proves asymptotic and depth-1 guarantees for Quantum MaxCut, derives iterative energy formulas on high-girth regular graphs, and benchmarks it numerically.

existing.note: The formal Conjecture 1 is only for the AFM Heisenberg XXX ring of size N (depth O(N)); the Discussion's wider wording (1d 2-local LHPs) rests on XY and XXZ ring numerics, which the authors say only 'suggests' the extension.
existing.value: The authors conjecture that for an AFM Heisenberg XXX ring there is a HamQAOA circuit of depth linear in the ring size that prepares its exact ground state, and state that their XXZ results suggest Conjecture 1 extends to more general local Hamiltonian problems.
existing.anchor: Conjecture 1, Sec. V B 2, p.14; Sec. V C, p.16; Sec. VI, p.16
quotes: Conjecture 1. For an AFM Heisenberg XXX ring of size
which prepares its exact ground state.
This suggests that Conjecture 1 extends to more general LHPs with richer ground state properties.
existing.certainty_reason: An unproven conjecture supported by small-ring numerics.

existing.note: The paper's guarantees are: Theorem 1 (exact QMC ground state as depth goes to infinity on bipartite graphs), Lemma 1 (depth 1 no worse than AGM on any graph and the SDP of [3] on edge-transitive graphs), and the iterative formula for average-case energy on high-girth regular graphs. Fuller value and quotes given; separate assertions below quote each.
existing.value: The authors establish rigorous guarantees for the HamQAOA on Quantum MaxCut: convergence to the exact ground state as depth goes to infinity on bipartite graphs, depth-one performance no worse than prior AGM and SDP algorithms, and an iterative formula for its average energy on high-girth regular graphs.

papers.title_in_file: Multiparticle quantum walks for distinguishing hard graphs
papers.version_note: arXiv:2501.03683v2 (20 Mar 2025). The text layer holds the paper twice; the first copy was read in full. The k and graph-size columns of Tables II-V are missing from the text layer and were read from page images (pp.6 and 10). Tables IV and V captions say 'input superposition states' while the text says they use localized inputs.
papers.what_it_is: A PASQAL study of k-particle continuous-time quantum walks under an XY Hamiltonian for graph isomorphism, arguing they distinguish k-CFI graphs (with superposition input) and SRGs (with localized input), with simulations up to k=3.

existing.note: The paper's argument is explicit only for k=2 (1-QW, at most 6 hops) and for 2-QW on 3-CFI graphs; the general k case is asserted by analogy ('can be seen also'). Simulations cover k=2 and 3 only.
existing.value: The authors argue that a single-particle walk with localized input distinguishes k=2 CFI graphs within 6 hops and that a 2-QW distinguishes 3-CFI graphs, state that the same contradiction extends to k-1 QW for general k-CFI graphs, and report simulations distinguishing k=2 and k=3 CFI graphs.

we show the empirical results for k=2 and k=3 CFI graphs using 1-QW and 2-QW respectively with localized input states and see that we are able to distinguish them using the HXY interaction.

operation ensures that ∆ is zero for isomorphic graphs.

The two graphs can be distinguished by the presence or absence of a 2-clique of size k+1.

assertions.value: The paper shows the smallest CFI pair (k equal to one) is trivially distinguished by its degree distribution.
quotes: Thus these graphs are trivially distinguished because of the difference in the degree distribution.
assertions.certainty_reason: Complete small-case argument given.

assertions.value: The authors report that k-QW under the XY Hamiltonian and non-interacting fermions give similar gap values, while non-interacting bosons give very low values, which they attribute to multiple occupation being forbidden for the first two but allowed for bosons.
assertions.anchor: Sec. III A, Tables II-III, pp.6-7
quotes: we obtain similar values of ∆ for evolution using HXY and noninteracting fermions, while obtaining very low values for non-interacting bosons.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report gaps with localized input (Table IV) of 6.4823 for the smaller CFI pair and 9.5073 for the k=3 pair, and that non-interacting particles give a much lower gap for k=3 CFI graphs (1.13e-13 and 1.25e-13).
assertions.anchor: Sec. III B, Table IV, p.10 (k column from page image)
quotes: a much lower value of ∆ is obtained for k=3 CFI graphs.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: Table IV and V captions say superposition input, conflicting with the text; Table V gives 4.8682 and 3.5894.

assertions.value: The authors argue, by an example of three-hop paths in a four-node clique, that a 2-QW with localized input counts quantities not determined by the SRG family parameters and hence can distinguish SRGs.
quotes: In this section we show that 2-QW counts quantities which are not only dependent on the SRG family parameters and hence can distinguish SRGs.
assertions.certainty_reason: Argument by example, not a general proof; no SRG simulations are reported.

assertions.value: The paper argues that with uniform superposition input every m-hop count in the 2-particle occupation graph is fixed by the SRG family parameters, so two SRGs of the same family cannot be distinguished by a 2-QW.
quotes: Hence two SRGs of the same family will have equal number of entries of a given value for any m-hop and hence cannot be distinguished by a 2-QW with input superposition state.
assertions.certainty_reason: A proof sketch by induction on hops.

assertions.value: The authors state that, like k-WL tests with time complexity of order N to the k, the number of quantities measured for k-QW with superposition input grows as N to the k, and for k − 1 QW with localized input as N to the power 2k − 2.
quotes: Similar to the k-WL tests which have time-complexity of O(N k),
superposition states goes as O(N k) while for k − 1QW with input localized states as O(N 2k−2).
assertions.certainty_reason: A stated scaling without derivation.
assertions.reader_inference: Exponents print flat in the text layer.

assertions.value: The authors (PASQAL) state that neutral-atom hardware can implement dynamics on an occupation graph of size of order N to the k by creating k excitations in an N-atom system, avoiding the storage k-WL needs, though this is experimentally challenging.
quotes: like neutral atoms can implement dynamics on an occupation graph G(k) of size O(N k) simply by creating k excitations in a N-atom system.
provide an interesting direction for a quantum advantage on graph-based practical problems of interest.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor describing its own platform's capability; no hardware run in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that uniform superposition inputs are experimentally challenging to create, though schemes with polynomial-time gates have been proposed.
quotes: experimentally challenging to create uniform superposition states, several schemes which require polynomial time gates have been proposed to create these states
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own stated limit.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that their results strongly suggest k-QW have similar distinguishing abilities and complexities as classical k-WL tests, and leave as an open problem how the gap scales with k.
quotes: that k-QW have similar distinguishing abilities and complexities as classical k-WL tests.
future problem of interest to see how the value of ∆ scales with k.
assertions.certainty_reason: An authors' concluding claim from small-k evidence.
